rules.rule_name: Clean Architecture and Separation of Concerns
rules.explanation: Writing monolithic UI classes that directly handle database queries, network calls, and business logic makes the mobile app unmaintainable and untestable.
rules.do: Implement Clean Architecture principles, cleanly separating UI components, ViewModels/Presenters, Domain use cases, and Data/Repository layers.
rules.dont: Do not mix UI rendering code directly with business logic or direct database/network fetching inside activity or view classes.

rules.rule_name: Predictable State Management and Unidirectional Data Flow
rules.explanation: Managing application state via scattered, mutable global variables leads to unpredictable UI bugs and race conditions.
rules.do: Adopt predictable state management frameworks (e.g., BLoC, Riverpod, Redux, Jetpack ViewModel with StateFlow) enforcing a unidirectional data flow (UDF).
rules.dont: Do not mutate global application states directly from arbitrary UI widgets without a controlled state pipeline.

rules.rule_name: Lifecycle-Aware Resource Management and Memory Leak Prevention
rules.explanation: Failing to release subscriptions, streams, or context references when mobile components destroy causes severe memory leaks and app crashes.
rules.do: Observe component lifecycles properly, dispose of controllers, streams, and listeners in `onDispose` or equivalent teardown methods.
rules.dont: Do not retain long-lived references to UI Context or View objects inside background threads or static singletons.

rules.rule_name: Modular UI Design and Component Reusability
rules.explanation: Building giant, monolithic screen layouts containing hundreds of lines of code reduces reusability and slows rendering performance.
rules.do: Break down user interfaces into small, stateless, reusable atomic widgets and composable design components.
rules.dont: Do not write massive single-file screen layouts that handle multiple unrelated layout sections.
